metaDescription: Frostclimb by HeyOggi Games: support, privacy policy and account deletion.
translationNote: This is a translation. If it differs from the English version, the English version applies.
intro: Jump, wall-bounce and chain combos to climb an icy tower across 30 frozen worlds. Free to play on iPhone, iPad and Android.
supportP: Questions, bug reports or purchase problems? E-mail us at {email}. Please include your device model and your player name. We usually reply within 2 business days.
q1: How do I keep my progress on a new phone?
a1: Open {settings} → {account} and sign in with Apple or Google. When you sign in with the same account on the new device, your progress and purchases come back.
q2: I bought something but didn’t receive it.
a2: Make sure you are signed in to the same Apple or Google account you used to buy, then restart the game. If it still doesn’t appear, e-mail us with the date of the purchase. Refunds are handled by Apple or Google Play.
q3: How do I change the controls?
a3: {settings} → {controls}: {oneHand}, {tilt} or {classic}. In {tilt} mode you can also choose the {sens}.
q4: How do I delete my data?
pIntro: This policy explains what information the Frostclimb mobile game (“the app”), published by HeyOggi Games (“we”), collects, why, and the choices you have. It applies to the iOS and Android versions of the app.
c1: Game account ID – an anonymous identifier created automatically by Google Firebase Authentication when you first play. Used to save your progress in the cloud and for the leaderboard.
c2: Sign-in details (optional) – if you link the game to Sign in with Apple or Google, we receive an account identifier and the e-mail address provided by that service (Apple may give a private relay address). Used to restore your progress and purchases on a new device.
c3: Player name (optional) – the name you type in {settings}. It is shown next to your score on the public leaderboard. If you don’t set one, a generic name such as “Player 4821” is used.
c4: Game data – progress, levels, stars, coins, scores, settings and purchased items. Used to run the game and sync it between your devices. Your best score and player name are visible to other players on the leaderboard.
c5: Purchase records – which in-app items you bought, so we can deliver and restore them. Payments are handled entirely by the App Store or Google Play; we never see your card or payment details.
c6: Advertising and device data – collected by the Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob): advertising ID, IP address (from which an approximate location is derived), device and app information, ad interactions, and crash/diagnostic data. Used to show and measure ads and to prevent fraud.
notCollected: We do not collect your precise location, contacts, photos, microphone or camera data. In {tilt} mode the app uses the phone’s motion sensor only while you play; this data stays on your device and is never sent anywhere.
pAds: The app shows ads from Google AdMob, including optional rewarded ads that you choose to watch. Where required (for example in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland), you are asked for consent through Google’s consent message, and you can change your choice later. On iOS, ads are personalised only if you allow tracking in Apple’s App Tracking Transparency prompt; otherwise non-personalised ads are shown. You can reset or delete your advertising ID in your device settings. If you buy “Remove Ads”, interstitial ads are no longer shown. How Google uses data: {googlePartner}.
pProviders: Google Firebase (Authentication, Cloud Firestore) stores your game account and cloud save; Google AdMob provides ads; Apple and Google provide sign-in and process in-app purchase payments. We do not sell your personal information and do not share it with anyone else, except where required by law.
pDevice: Your progress and settings are also stored on your device so that the game works offline. Uninstalling the app removes this copy.
pRetention: Your cloud save and leaderboard entry are kept until you delete them. Advertising data is kept by Google under its own policies.
pDelete: You can delete your data in the app at any time: {settings} → {account}, then {deleteAccount} (if you signed in with Apple or Google) or {deleteData} (if you play as a guest). This permanently removes your cloud save, your leaderboard entry and your game account. You can also ask us by e-mail; see {deleteLink}. E-mail requests are completed within 30 days.
pSecurity: All data is sent over encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS). Access to cloud saves is restricted so that each player can only read and change their own data.
pChildren: Frostclimb is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child under 13 has given us personal information, contact us and we will delete it.
pRights: Depending on where you live (for example under the GDPR or Turkey’s KVKK), you may have the right to access, correct, delete or export your personal data, to object to or restrict its processing, and to withdraw consent. Contact us to use these rights. You can also complain to your local data protection authority.
pChanges: We may update this policy. The effective date at the top shows the latest version; important changes will also be announced in the app.
step3: At the bottom, tap {deleteAccount} (if you signed in with Apple or Google) or {deleteData} (if you play as a guest), then confirm.
opt2P: Send an e-mail to {email} with the subject “Frostclimb account deletion”. Include your player name as shown on the leaderboard and the sign-in method you used, if any (Apple or Google, and its e-mail address). We will confirm and complete the deletion within 30 days.
del1: Your game account (Firebase account ID and linked Apple or Google sign-in, if any)
del2: Your cloud save and the progress stored on your device: levels, stars, coins, settings and purchased items
del3: Your player name and scores on the leaderboard
keptP: Nothing is kept by us after deletion. Purchase receipts remain with Apple or Google for their own records, and advertising data is handled by Google under its own policies. Deleting your account does not cancel or refund purchases, and items bought with it cannot be restored afterwards.
